subject: Which test statistic to use with WLSMV estimation?

messages.author: b1e2ae48042fca9f
messages.subject: Which test statistic to use with WLSMV estimation?
parts:
HI there, according to the lavaan Options documentation....
"the estimators "WLSM" and "WLSMV" imply the "DWLS" estimator (not the "WLS" estimator) with robust standard errors and a mean or mean and variance adjusted test statistic."
However, the previous paragraph states that there are two possible mean- and variance-adjusted test statistics available, one being the Satterthwaite style "mean.var.adjusted" and one being "scaled.shifted". Does anyone have advice on which to select?

Previously, I had estimator = "WLSMV" and test = "robust" (as I was following the advice of a tutor), but now I'm not so sure that the test option I've selected is correct?

Thanks
Victoria

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Which test statistic to use with WLSMV estimation?
parts:
according to the lavaan Options documentation....
"the estimators "WLSM" and "WLSMV" imply the "DWLS" estimator (not the "WLS" estimator) with robust standard errors and a mean or mean and variance adjusted test statistic."
However, the previous paragraph states that there are two possible mean- and variance-adjusted test statistics available, one being the Satterthwaite style "mean.var.adjusted" and one being "scaled.shifted". Does anyone have advice on which to select?

The default is "scaled.shifted", I believe because it is more efficient than the Satterthwaite approach.

http://www.statmodel.com/download/webnotes/webnote10.pdf
 
test = "robust" 

That is not an option (does not appear in documentation).  Both "mean.var.adjusted" and "scaled.shifted" are robust options available with DWLS estimation.
